page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Gen9 processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.44 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.31 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2351.0. Memory performance is also notable, with a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3604.52 and cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 1085.97 GB/sec. Multi-core performance falls in the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 16026.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12853.0.

In terms of specialized workloads, the c9g.2xlarge shows average performance in static web serving at 28.89 GB/sec, Redis SET operations at 24.48 million operations per second, and software compilation. For machine learning tasks, it achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 345.69 tokens per second with a small 135M LLM model, though performance drops to a weaker 22.52 tokens per second for prompt processing on medium 7B models. Cryptographic operations represent a relative bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical cores and high single-threaded performance offer strong value for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The instance is highly suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
